provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Living and non living
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify living things.
The pupils should be able to identify non living things.
Introduction:
Last week we learned about our body parts.
Today we learn about things that are alive.
Content:
Living things grow. A dog grows big. A plant grows tall.
Living things need food. A plant needs water.
Non living things do not grow. A stone stays small.
Non living things do not eat. A table does not eat.
Class activity:
Let's sort picture cards into living and non living piles.
Evaluation questions:
What does a plant need?
Does a stone grow?
Is a dog living or non living?
Summary:
Living things grow and eat. Non living things do not.

topics.title: Parts of a plant
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name the parts of a plant.
The pupils should be able to point to each part on a plant.
Introduction:
Last week we learned about living things.
Plants are living things with special parts.
Content:
Roots are under the soil. They drink water.
Stem holds the plant up. It is like a neck.
Leaves make food for the plant. They are green.
Flowers make seeds. They are beautiful.
Class activity:
Each child touches the parts on a real plant.
Evaluation questions:
Which part is under the soil?
What color are the leaves?
What does the stem do?
Summary:
Plants have roots, stem, leaves and flowers.

topics.title: Animals and their homes
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name animal homes.
The pupils should be able to match animals to their homes.
Introduction:
Last week we learned about plant parts.
Animals also have special places to live.
Content:
A dog lives in a kennel. It is like a small house.
A bird lives in a nest. It is made of sticks.
A fish lives in water. It is called a pond.
A cow lives in a pen. It is like a big cage.
Class activity:
Let's match picture cards of animals to their homes.
Evaluation questions:
Where does a bird live?
What does a dog live in?
Name an animal that lives in water.
Summary:
Different animals live in different homes.

topics.title: Animal babies
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name animal babies.
The pupils should be able to match mothers to babies.
Introduction:
Last week we learned about animal homes.
Today we learn about animal babies and their mothers.
Content:
A cow has a calf. The calf drinks milk.
A hen has a chick. The chick is small and yellow.
A cat has a kitten. The kitten plays with yarn.
A dog has a puppy. The puppy is cute.
Class activity:
Let's match picture cards of mothers to their babies.
Evaluation questions:
What is a baby cow called?
What does a chick look like?
Name a baby animal.
Summary:
Animal babies have special names.

topics.title: Float and sink
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to predict if objects will float or sink.
The pupils should be able to test objects in water.
Introduction:
Last week we learned about animal babies.
Today we learn about things in water.
Content:
Some things float on water. A boat floats.
Some things sink in water. A stone sinks.
Heavy things usually sink. A nail sinks.
Light things usually float. A leaf floats.
Class activity:
Let's drop objects in water and guess if they float or sink.
Evaluation questions:
What happens to a stone in water?
What happens to a boat in water?
Why do some things float?
Summary:
Things can float or sink in water.

topics.title: Air is everywhere
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to show that air exists.
The pupils should be able to feel moving air.
Introduction:
Last week we learned about floating and sinking.
Today we learn about air all around us.
Content:
Air is all around us. We cannot see it.
Air makes the wind blow. We can feel it.
Air fills balloons. Balloons get big.
Air helps us breathe. We need air to live.
Class activity:
Let's blow bubbles and feel the wind on our faces.
Evaluation questions:
Can we see air?
What does air make?
Why do we need air?
Summary:
Air is everywhere but we cannot see it.

topics.title: Day and night sky
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name things in the day sky.
The pupils should be able to name things in the night sky.
Introduction:
Last week we learned about air.
The sky looks different in the day and at night.
Content:
In the day sky we see the sun. The sun is bright.
In the day sky we see clouds. Clouds are white.
In the night sky we see the moon. The moon is round.
In the night sky we see stars. Stars twinkle.
Class activity:
Let's draw the night sky with stars and moon.
Evaluation questions:
What do we see in the day sky?
What do we see in the night sky?
Is the sun out at night?
Summary:
The day sky has sun and clouds. The night sky has moon and stars.

topics.title: Rainy and sunny days
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name clothes for rainy days.
The pupils should be able to name clothes for sunny days.
Introduction:
Last week we learned about day and night.
Today we learn about rainy and sunny days.
Content:
On rainy days we wear raincoats. Raincoats keep us dry.
On rainy days we wear rain boots. Rain boots keep our feet dry.
On sunny days we wear hats. Hats keep our heads cool.
On sunny days we wear sunglasses. Sunglasses protect our eyes.
Class activity:
Let's dress up for rainy and sunny days.
Evaluation questions:
What do we wear when it rains?
What do we wear when the sun is hot?
Why do we need umbrellas?
Summary:
We wear different clothes for rainy and sunny days.

topics.title: Sound around us
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify loud and soft sounds.
The pupils should be able to make different sounds.
Introduction:
Last week we learned about rainy and sunny days.
Today we learn about sounds we hear every day.
Content:
Some sounds are loud. A drum is loud.
Some sounds are soft. A whisper is soft.
We can make sounds with our mouths.
We can make sounds with instruments.
Class activity:
Let's make sounds with bottles and drums.
Evaluation questions:
Is a whisper loud or soft?
What makes a loud sound?
How can we make sound?
Summary:
Sounds can be loud or soft.

topics.title: Revision and discovery fair
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to show their favorite discovery.
The pupils should be able to sort living and non living things.
Introduction:
This week we revise all we learned this term.
We will have a discovery fair to show what we know.
Content:\Living things grow and eat. Non living things do not.
Plants have roots, stem, leaves and flowers.
Animals live in different homes.
Animal babies have special names.
Things can float or sink in water.
Air is all around us but we cannot see it.
The day sky has sun and clouds. The night sky has moon and stars.
We wear different clothes for rainy and sunny days.
Sounds can be loud or soft.
Class activity:
Each child shows their favorite discovery and tells the class about it.
Then we sort living and non living things into two groups.
Evaluation questions:
What did you like learning most?
Can you name a living thing?
Can you name a non living thing?
What do plants need to grow?
Summary:
We learned many wonderful things about our world this term.
